Buying guide · Thickness

Condom thickness compared: 0.01, 0.03 and 0.04 mm

The millimetre figure on a condom box is the thickness of the film itself. A smaller number feels less intrusive; a larger one has more presence, and leaves more room for studs and texture. Thickness, though, is not the same thing as safety.

Last updated 2026-11-05

On this page
  1. The number is the thickness of the film
  2. What thin and thick actually change
  3. The thickness of the four T-ZERO designs
  4. Which thickness to choose

The number is the thickness of the film

A condom is moulded as a thin film and then cut to length. A figure like "0.03 mm" on the box is the thickness of that film as it is made — not the length, and not the width. Every condom in a box varies slightly; the printed figure is an average.

Thickness Where you meet it How it feels Worth knowing
0.01 – 0.02 mm Ultra thin You barely notice the film is there Harder to make, but the leak test is the same
0.03 mm Thin Light presence, and warmth comes through The balance between thinness and durability
0.04 mm Medium More noticeable Enough material for raised studs
0.06 – 0.08 mm Standard The most common thickness Most condoms people use are in this range

What thin and thick actually change

Thickness changes the feel, not the function. There are four places you can feel it:

  • Presence — the thinner the film, the closer it is to wearing nothing at all.
  • Warmth — a thinner film carries body heat through faster and insulates less.
  • Durability — a thinner film has less margin against friction and stretching over a long time, so a fresh one is the safer choice.
  • Room for texture — studs, wrinkles and ribs need extra material, so textured products are normally thicker.

Thicker does not mean safer

A lot of people assume thicker means safer. The burst pressure and tensile strength of a genuine condom are governed by an international standard, ISO 4071, and every condom is electronically tested for holes. A thinner film is not more likely to fail. Thickness changes the feel, not the safety.

The thickness of the four T-ZERO designs

Design Thickness Why this thickness
Ultra Thin 0.01 mm For the feel of very nearly nothing, and for warmth to come through quickly
Extended 0.03 mm A balance between warmth and fit that still holds up over a long time
Extra Lubricant 0.03 mm A thin film with a hyaluronic lubricant layer — the emphasis is on lubrication, not on thickness
Studded 0.04 mm Raised studs need enough material to hold their shape, and they sit more evenly

All four are made of the same material — medical-grade natural latex — and every condom is electronically leak tested. The thickness differs; the standard does not. All four are sold at Watsons and HKTVmall.

Which thickness to choose

Most people should not deliberate for long: start with a middle-of-the-road box, settle the size and the material, and move to a thinner or a more textured one afterwards if you want to.

  • For the least sensation, close to wearing nothing → Ultra Thin, 0.01 mm.
  • For a steady fit over a longer stretch → Extended or Extra Lubricant, 0.03 mm.
  • For extra sensation → Studded, 0.04 mm.
  • Still deciding → read the first-time guide and start with the size.

Frequently asked questions

Is a 0.01 mm condom safe?

Yes. The burst pressure and tensile strength of a genuine condom are governed by ISO 4071, each batch is tested and every condom is electronically checked for holes. The 0.01 mm figure describes the thickness of the film, not the standard it is held to.

Does a thicker condom last longer?

Generally a thicker film has more margin against friction and stretching, so it is less likely to break over a long time. But a condom is a single-use product: whatever the thickness, a new one every time is what actually works.

Is 0.03 mm ultra thin?

It counts as thin, but not as ultra thin. The most common condoms are around 0.06 to 0.08 mm, so 0.03 mm is clearly thinner than usual. The T-ZERO Ultra Thin is 0.01 mm, which is in the ultra-thin range.

At the same price, should I buy the thinner one or the thicker one?

Start with what you are using it for. Buying for the first time, or using it now and then, a thinner style keeps the feel to a minimum; for longer sessions or extra sensation, a thicker textured one is the more practical choice.
